title: The colourful star cluster NGC 3590
caption: The star cluster NGC 3590, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Bright stars shine out in front of a dramatic backdrop: dark patches of dust and richly coloured clouds of glowing gas. The stars belong to NGC 3590, a small star cluster photographed at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile using the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope.

A star cluster like this is a family of stars born together from the same cloud of material. Because its members share a birthplace and roughly an age, the cluster works as a natural experiment, letting astronomers compare how stars of different masses develop over time. ESO notes that this modest gathering offers clues to how its stars formed and how they are changing.

It also has something to say about the bigger picture. The Milky Way is a spiral with arms that wind around its centre, and our place inside the disc makes their layout hard to map. Clusters such as NGC 3590 give astronomers hints about the structure of those pinwheeling arms.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, using blue, visual, red and hydrogen-alpha filters in visible light. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye, bringing out faint glowing gas and dust that would be invisible through a telescope eyepiece.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: Besides the cluster itself, the frame takes in dark patches of dust and clouds of glowing gas. The picture was made with the Wide Field Imager camera, through blue, visual, red and hydrogen-alpha filters.
alt: Bright stars of a small cluster in front of dark dust patches and colourful glowing gas clouds.
